chapters.name: Thermal Physics
chapters.description: Study of kinetic particle model of matter, states of matter, thermal properties, temperature, and transfer of thermal energy through conduction, convection, and radiation.

lessons.name: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter | States of Matter
lessons.description: Understanding distinguishing properties of solids, liquids and gases, knowing terms for changes in state (melting, boiling, condensing, freezing, evaporating)

lessons.name: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter | Molecular Matter
lessons.description: Understanding particle structure of solids, liquids and gases in terms of arrangement, separation and motion, representing states using simple particle diagrams

lessons.name: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter | Particle Model of Gases
lessons.description: Understanding pressure in gases in terms of particle motion and collisions, forces exerted by particles, relationship between particle motion and temperature

lessons.name: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter | Brownian Motion
lessons.description: Understanding Brownian motion as evidence for kinetic particle model, describing and explaining random motion in terms of collisions between microscopic particles in suspension and gas or liquid particles

lessons.name: Kinetic Particle Model of Matter | Gases & Absolute Temperature
lessons.description: Understanding effect of temperature and volume changes on gas pressure, absolute zero (−273°C), converting between Kelvin and Celsius T(K) = θ(°C) + 273, using pV = constant

lessons.name: Thermal Properties & Temperature | Thermal Expansion
lessons.description: Understanding thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases at constant pressure, everyday applications and consequences, explaining expansion in terms of particle motion

lessons.name: Thermal Properties & Temperature | Specific Heat Capacity
lessons.description: Understanding that temperature rise increases internal energy and average kinetic energy, defining specific heat capacity c = ∆E/(m∆θ), using the equation in calculations

lessons.name: Thermal Properties & Temperature | Investigating Specific Heat Capacity
lessons.description: Experimental measurement of specific heat capacity for solids and liquids, practical procedures, analyzing results and calculating specific heat capacity from experimental data

lessons.name: Thermal Properties & Temperature | Melting & Boiling
lessons.description: Understanding melting and boiling as energy input without temperature change, melting and boiling points of water, describing condensation and solidification in terms of particles

lessons.name: Thermal Properties & Temperature | Evaporation
lessons.description: Understanding evaporation as escape of more-energetic particles from liquid surface, differences between boiling and evaporation, factors affecting evaporation rate, evaporative cooling

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | Demonstrating Conduction
lessons.description: Experiments to demonstrate properties of good thermal conductors and bad thermal conductors (thermal insulators), practical demonstrations and observations

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | Thermal Conduction
lessons.description: Understanding thermal conduction in terms of lattice vibrations and free electrons in metals, why gases and liquids are poor conductors, range of thermal conductors

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | Convection
lessons.description: Understanding convection as thermal energy transfer in liquids and gases, explaining convection in terms of density changes, experimental demonstration of convection

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | Radiation
lessons.description: Understanding thermal radiation as infrared radiation, all objects emit infrared, radiation doesn't require a medium, effect of surface color and texture on emission, absorption and reflection

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | The Greenhouse Effect
lessons.description: Understanding thermal equilibrium when energy received equals energy transferred away, effect on Earth's temperature, how factors control balance between incoming and emitted radiation, rate of emission depends on surface temperature and area

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | Investigating IR Radiation
lessons.description: Experiments to distinguish between good and bad emitters of infrared radiation, experiments to distinguish between good and bad absorbers of infrared radiation, practical investigations

lessons.name: Transfer of Thermal Energy | Consequences of Thermal Energy Transfer
lessons.description: Explaining everyday applications and consequences of conduction, convection and radiation: heating pans, heating rooms, fires burning fuel, car radiators, where multiple types of thermal energy transfer are significant

chapters.name: Waves
chapters.description: General properties of waves, light (reflection, refraction, thin lenses, dispersion), electromagnetic spectrum, and sound waves including their characteristics and applications.

lessons.name: General Properties of Waves | Features of Waves
lessons.description: Understanding that waves transfer energy without transferring matter, wave features (wavefront, wavelength, frequency, amplitude, wave speed), describing wave motion

lessons.name: General Properties of Waves | The Wave Equation
lessons.description: Using v = fλ for wave speed calculations, understanding the relationship between speed, frequency and wavelength, applying the equation to various wave problems

lessons.name: General Properties of Waves | Transverse & Longitudinal Waves
lessons.description: Understanding transverse waves (electromagnetic radiation, water waves, S-waves) and longitudinal waves (sound, P-waves), direction of vibration vs propagation

lessons.name: General Properties of Waves | Wave Behaviour
lessons.description: Understanding wave reflection at plane surfaces, refraction due to speed changes, diffraction through gaps and at edges, how wavelength and gap size affect diffraction

lessons.name: General Properties of Waves | Ripple Tank
lessons.description: Using ripple tank to demonstrate reflection at plane surface, refraction due to change in depth, diffraction due to gap and edge, experimental observations and techniques

lessons.name: Light | Reflection of Light
lessons.description: Defining normal, angle of incidence and angle of reflection, law of reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection), image formation by plane mirrors

lessons.name: Light | Investigating Reflection
lessons.description: Simple constructions, measurements and calculations for reflection by plane mirrors, experimental determination of angles, practical investigations

lessons.name: Light | Refraction of Light
lessons.description: Understanding refraction at boundaries, passage through transparent materials, experimental demonstration with blocks of different shapes, defining angle of refraction

lessons.name: Light | Refractive Index
lessons.description: Defining refractive index as ratio of wave speeds, using n = sin i / sin r, calculating refractive index from experimental data

lessons.name: Light | Total Internal Reflection
lessons.description: Understanding critical angle, internal and total internal reflection, using n = 1/sin c, applications in optical fibres for telecommunications

lessons.name: Light | Ray Diagrams
lessons.description: Drawing ray diagrams for thin converging and diverging lenses, understanding focal length, principal axis and principal focus, ray diagram conventions

lessons.name: Light | Real & Virtual Images
lessons.description: Understanding characteristics of images using terms enlarged/same size/diminished, upright/inverted and real/virtual, knowing virtual image formed when diverging rays are extrapolated backwards

lessons.name: Light | Real Images
lessons.description: Action of converging lenses on parallel beams, ray diagrams for formation of real images by converging lens, calculating image positions and characteristics

lessons.name: Light | Virtual Images
lessons.description: Action of diverging lenses, virtual image formation with converging lenses, ray diagrams for virtual images, describing use of single lens as magnifying glass

lessons.name: Light | Correcting Sight
lessons.description: Using converging and diverging lenses to correct long-sightedness and short-sightedness, understanding how lenses correct vision defects, applications of lenses in corrective eyewear

lessons.name: Light | Dispersion of Light
lessons.description: Understanding dispersion by glass prism, seven colors of visible spectrum in order of frequency and wavelength, monochromatic light

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum | Electromagnetic Waves
lessons.description: Understanding main regions of electromagnetic spectrum in order of frequency and wavelength, all EM waves travel at same speed in vacuum (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s)

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum | Uses of Electromagnetic Waves
lessons.description: Understanding typical uses of radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays in various applications

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum | Dangers of Electromagnetic Waves
lessons.description: Understanding harmful effects of excessive exposure to microwaves, infrared, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays on living tissue

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum | Communications
lessons.description: Understanding satellite communications (low orbit and geostationary), mobile phones, wireless internet, Bluetooth, optical fibres, systems of communication relying on electromagnetic radiation

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum | Digital & Analogue Signals
lessons.description: Understanding difference between digital and analogue signals, sound transmitted as digital or analogue signal, benefits of digital signalling including increased rate of transmission and range

lessons.name: Sound | Sound Waves
lessons.description: Understanding production of sound by vibrating sources, longitudinal nature of sound, audible frequency range (20 Hz to 20 kHz), sound requires a medium, speed of sound in air (≈330-350 m/s)

lessons.name: Sound | Measuring the Speed of Sound
lessons.description: Understanding compression and rarefaction, methods for determining speed of sound using distance and time measurements, sound travels faster in solids than liquids, faster in liquids than gases

lessons.name: Sound | Effects of Sound Waves
lessons.description: Understanding how amplitude and frequency affect loudness and pitch of sound waves, echoes as reflection of sound

lessons.name: Sound | Ultrasound
lessons.description: Defining ultrasound as sound with frequency higher than 20 kHz, uses in non-destructive testing of materials, medical scanning of soft tissue and sonar including calculations

chapters.name: Electricity and Magnetism
chapters.description: Comprehensive study of magnetism, electrical quantities, electric circuits, electrical safety, and electromagnetic effects including induction, generators, motors and transformers.

lessons.name: Simple Phenomena of Magnetism | Magnetism
lessons.description: Describing forces between magnetic poles and between magnets and magnetic materials, using terms north pole, south pole, attraction, repulsion, magnetised and unmagnetised

lessons.name: Simple Phenomena of Magnetism | Magnets
lessons.description: Understanding induced magnetism, differences between temporary magnets (soft iron) and permanent magnets (steel), difference between magnetic and non-magnetic materials

lessons.name: Simple Phenomena of Magnetism | Magnetic Fields
lessons.description: Describing magnetic field as region where magnetic pole experiences force, understanding direction of magnetic field at a point, uses of permanent magnets and electromagnets

lessons.name: Simple Phenomena of Magnetism | Plotting Magnetic Fields
lessons.description: Drawing pattern and direction of magnetic field lines around bar magnet, plotting with compass and iron filings, using compass to determine direction, field strength represented by spacing

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Electric Charge
lessons.description: Understanding positive and negative charges, attraction and repulsion, electrostatic charging by friction, detection of charges, charging involves transfer of electrons only

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Demonstrating Electric Charges
lessons.description: Simple experiments to show production of electrostatic charges by friction, experiments to show detection of electrostatic charges, practical demonstrations

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Electric Fields
lessons.description: Understanding electric field as region where charge experiences force, direction of field on positive charge, field patterns around point charges, charged spheres, and parallel plates, charge measured in coulombs

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Investigating Conductors & Insulators
lessons.description: Experiment to distinguish between electrical conductors and insulators, using electron model to explain difference, giving typical examples of each

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Current
lessons.description: Understanding current as flow of charge, defining current I = Q/t, using ammeters (analogue and digital), conduction in metals via free electrons, conventional vs electron flow

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Direct & Alternating Current
lessons.description: Understanding difference between direct current (d.c.) and alternating current (a.c.), characteristics of each type, applications of DC and AC

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Electromotive Force
lessons.description: Defining electromotive force (e.m.f.) as electrical work done by source in moving unit charge around complete circuit, measured in volts, using E = W/Q

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Potential Difference
lessons.description: Defining potential difference (p.d.) as work done by unit charge passing through component, measured in volts, using V = W/Q, using voltmeters with different ranges

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Resistance
lessons.description: Using R = V/I, experimental determination of resistance using voltmeter and ammeter, qualitative relationship of resistance to length and cross-sectional area of wire

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Resistance of a Wire
lessons.description: Sketching and explaining current-voltage graphs for resistors, filament lamps and diodes, resistance proportional to length and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Electrical Energy
lessons.description: Understanding energy transfer in circuits from source to circuit components to surroundings, using E = IVt for electrical energy, calculating energy transferred

lessons.name: Electrical Quantities | Electrical Power
lessons.description: Using P = IV for electrical power, defining kilowatt-hour (kW h), calculating cost of using electrical appliances where energy unit is kW h

lessons.name: Electric Circuits & Electrical Safety | Circuit Diagrams & Circuit Components
lessons.description: Drawing and interpreting circuit diagrams with cells, batteries, switches, resistors, thermistors, LDRs, lamps, motors, ammeters, voltmeters, diodes, LEDs, understanding component behavior

lessons.name: Electric Circuits & Electrical Safety | Current in Circuits
lessons.description: Understanding current at every point in series circuit is same, current from source larger than in each branch for parallel circuits, junction rule, constructing and using circuits

lessons.name: Electric Circuits & Electrical Safety | EMF & Potential Difference in Circuits
lessons.description: Calculating combined e.m.f. of sources in series, understanding p.d. across components in series and parallel, p.d. across parallel branches, sum of p.d.s equals total e.m.f.

lessons.name: Electric Circuits & Electrical Safety | Combined Resistance
lessons.description: Calculating combined resistance of resistors in series, calculating combined resistance of two resistors in parallel, understanding combined resistance in parallel is less than individual resistors

lessons.name: Electric Circuits & Electrical Safety | Potential Dividers
lessons.description: Understanding how p.d. increases with resistance for constant current, action of variable potential divider, using R₁/R₂ = V₁/V₂ for potential divider calculations

lessons.name: Electric Circuits & Electrical Safety | Electrical Safety
lessons.description: Understanding hazards of damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions, excess current, live/neutral/earth wires, switches on live wire, fuses and trip switches, earthing vs double insulation

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Electromagnetic Induction
lessons.description: Understanding that moving conductor across magnetic field or changing field induces e.m.f., factors affecting magnitude of induced e.m.f., direction opposes change (Lenz's law)

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Demonstrating Induction
lessons.description: Experimental demonstration of electromagnetic induction, practical techniques, observing and analyzing induced e.m.f. in various situations

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | The A.C. Generator
lessons.description: Understanding simple AC generator (rotating coil or magnet), slip rings and brushes, sketching e.m.f. vs time graphs, relating coil position to peaks, troughs and zeros

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Magnetic Effect of a Current
lessons.description: Understanding magnetic field patterns around straight wires and solenoids, use in relays and loudspeakers, effect of changing current magnitude and direction

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Investigating the Field Around a Wire
lessons.description: Experiment to identify pattern of magnetic field (including direction) due to currents in straight wires and solenoids, qualitative variation of field strength, practical investigation

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor
lessons.description: Understanding force on conductor in magnetic field, effect of reversing current or field direction, relative directions of force, field and current (Fleming's Left Hand Rule), force on charged particle beams

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Electric Motors
lessons.description: Understanding turning effect on current-carrying coil in magnetic field, increasing effect by more turns, higher current, stronger field, operation with split-ring commutator and brushes

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Transformers
lessons.description: Understanding transformer construction with soft-iron core, primary and secondary coils, step-up and step-down transformers, using Vp/Vs = Np/Ns, principle of operation

lessons.name: Electromagnetic Effects | Transformer Calculations
lessons.description: Using transformers in high-voltage transmission, advantages of high-voltage transmission, using IpVp = IsVs for 100% efficiency, using P = I²R to explain reduced power losses

chapters.name: Nuclear Physics
chapters.description: Study of atomic structure, the nuclear model, composition of the nucleus, isotopes, radioactivity, detection, types of emissions, decay, half-life, and safety precautions.

lessons.name: The Nuclear Model of the Atom | The Atom
lessons.description: Understanding atom structure with positively charged nucleus and negatively charged electrons in orbit, how atoms form positive and negative ions by losing or gaining electrons

lessons.name: The Nuclear Model of the Atom | The Nucleus
lessons.description: Understanding how alpha particle scattering supports nuclear model: very small nucleus, mostly empty space, nucleus contains most mass, nucleus is positively charged

lessons.name: The Nuclear Model of the Atom | Protons, Neutrons & Electrons
lessons.description: Understanding nucleus composition (protons and neutrons), relative charges (+1, 0, -1), defining proton number Z and nucleon number A, calculating neutrons, using nuclide notation, understanding isotopes

lessons.name: The Nuclear Model of the Atom | Fission & Fusion
lessons.description: Understanding nuclear fission (splitting) and fusion (joining) processes, nuclide equations, mass and energy changes, qualitative descriptions of energy release

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Background Radiation
lessons.description: Understanding background radiation, sources making significant contributions (radon gas, rocks and buildings, food and drink, cosmic rays), measuring with detectors and counters, count rate, corrected count rate

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Types of Radiation
lessons.description: Understanding emission as spontaneous and random, identifying alpha, beta and gamma emissions by nature, relative ionising effects, relative penetrating abilities, deflection in electric and magnetic fields

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Ionising Power & Deflection
lessons.description: Explaining ionising effects with reference to kinetic energy and electric charge of different radiations, understanding deflection patterns in fields

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Radioactive Decay
lessons.description: Understanding radioactive decay as change in unstable nucleus, spontaneous and random nature, emission of alpha, beta and/or gamma, nucleus changes to different element, why isotopes are radioactive, using decay equations with nuclide notation

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Half-Life
lessons.description: Defining half-life as time for half the nuclei to decay, using definition in calculations with tables and decay curves, calculating half-life from data where background radiation has or has not been subtracted

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Uses of Radiation
lessons.description: Understanding how radiation type and half-life determine applications: smoke alarms, irradiating food, sterilisation, thickness control, cancer diagnosis and treatment, linking penetration and absorption to applications

lessons.name: Radioactivity | Dangers of Radiation
lessons.description: Understanding effects of ionising radiation on living things (cell death, mutations, cancer), how to move, use and store radioactive materials safely, safety precautions (time, distance, shielding)

chapters.name: Space Physics
chapters.description: Study of Earth and the Solar System, planetary motion, orbital mechanics, the Sun as a star, stellar life cycles, the Universe, galaxies, redshift, and the Big Bang theory.

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | The Earth, Moon & Sun
lessons.description: Understanding Earth as planet rotating on tilted axis once per ~24 hours (explaining daily Sun motion and day/night cycle), orbiting Sun once per ~365 days (explaining seasons), Moon orbits Earth once per ~1 month explaining Moon phases

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | The Solar System
lessons.description: Understanding Solar System contains one star (Sun), eight named planets in order, minor planets (dwarf planets like Pluto, asteroids), moons orbiting planets, smaller bodies (comets, natural satellites), comparing inner rocky planets with outer gaseous planets

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | Formation of the Solar System
lessons.description: Understanding accretion model for Solar System formation (gravity, elements in interstellar clouds, rotating disc formation), explaining why inner planets are rocky and small, outer planets are gaseous and large

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | Light Speed Calculations
lessons.description: Calculating time for light to travel significant distances between Solar System objects, understanding light-speed delays in space communication

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | Gravitational Field Strength
lessons.description: Understanding gravitational field strength at planet surface depends on mass, decreases with distance from planet, Sun contains most Solar System mass (explaining why planets orbit Sun), analyzing planetary data about gravitational field

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | Orbital Speed Equation
lessons.description: Defining average orbital speed using v = 2πr/T where r is average orbit radius and T is orbital period, using equation in calculations, understanding orbital speeds decrease with distance from Sun

lessons.name: Earth & The Solar System | Elliptical Orbits
lessons.description: Understanding planets, minor planets and comets have elliptical orbits (Sun not at centre except for circular orbits), objects in elliptical orbits travel faster when closer to Sun (conservation of energy)

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | The Sun as a Star
lessons.description: Understanding Sun as medium-sized star consisting mostly of hydrogen and helium, radiates energy in infrared, visible and ultraviolet regions, powered by nuclear fusion (hydrogen → helium) in stable stars

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | The Scale of the Universe
lessons.description: Understanding galaxies contain many billions of stars, Sun is in Milky Way galaxy, other stars much further from Earth than Sun, astronomical distances measured in light-years (one light-year = 9.5 × 10¹⁵ m), Milky Way diameter approximately 100,000 light-years, Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies in Universe

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | Star Formation
lessons.description: Understanding star formation from interstellar clouds of gas and dust containing hydrogen, protostar as collapsing cloud increasing in temperature, stable star when gravitational force balanced by outward force from high temperature

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | Life Cycle of a Star
lessons.description: Understanding stars run out of hydrogen fuel, less massive stars expand to red giants then form planetary nebula with white dwarf, massive stars expand to red supergiants, supernova explosion forms nebula leaving neutron star or black hole, nebula may form new stars with planets

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | Galactic Redshift
lessons.description: Understanding redshift as increase in wavelength of EM radiation from receding stars/galaxies, light from distant galaxies appears redshifted compared to Earth, speed v of galaxy from redshift, distance d from supernova brightness

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | The Big Bang Theory
lessons.description: Understanding redshift is evidence Universe is expanding and supports Big Bang theory, CMBR is microwave radiation observed everywhere produced shortly after Universe formed, radiation expanded into microwave region as Universe expanded

lessons.name: Stars & The Universe | Age of the Universe
lessons.description: Defining Hubble constant H₀ = v/d, current estimate H₀ = 2.2 × 10⁻¹⁸ per second, understanding d/v = 1/H₀ estimates age of Universe (evidence for Big Bang), calculating age of Universe
